{"Author":"Valenth Siveria","Name":"Throw Crap Out","Punchline":"Don't carry your old stuff around","Description":"Wiht ThrowCrapOut (/tco) you can sort, clear out and free your Space in your Armoury. It allows you to sort your Armoury and pull out Gear not assigned to a Gearset.


Features:
- Sort = Just sorts your Gear in your Armoury by Item Level descending.
- Split = Basically like Sort, but moving Non-Gearset Gear to the end Slots of each Category.
- Clear = Pulls out your Non-Gearset Gear out of your Armoury to your Inventory.

Allows to clear out one category by another (default) or just taking the highest Item Level of Non-Gearset Gear one after another across the Categories to your Inventory.


Define a limit of free Inventory Space to keep, if you have way too much old gear stuff in your Armoury.


Define, which Categories should be handled, and which not.


Visual feedback for the sorting. Never guess anymore, how unsorted and chaotic your Armoury maybe looks like. TCO will take care of it.


Commands:


- /tco
- /tco settings
- /tco sort
- /tco split
- /tco clear

{"Author":"Aida Enna","Name":"Macro Chain Redux","Description":"Allows for a macro to continue onto the next macro by using '/nextmacro' on the last line of a macro.
Adding '/nextmacro' on the last line of Macro #01 will automatically execute Macro #02
Adding '/nextmacro down' on the last line of Macro #01 will automatically execute Macro #11
Also allows executing any macro from chat using '/runmacro'

{"Author":"The Combat Reborn Team","Name":"Rotation Solver Reborn","InternalName":"RotationSolver","Description":"Analyses combat information every frame and finds the best action.

This means almost all the information available in one frame in combat, including the status of all players in the party, the status of any hostile targets, skill cooldowns, the MP and HP of characters, the location of characters, casting status of the hostile target, combo, combat duration, player level, etc.

ITEM GATHERER — Pull designated items off your retainers into your bags, optionally returning your market listings first. Manual withdraw/deposit actions included.

BUYER — Build a shopping list by hand or import a MakePlace furniture list, then SCAN the market per world via Universalis and press SEND to travel with Lifestream and buy across worlds. Every purchase is verified against the game's own confirmation dialog before it is accepted. Listings are bought whole, so by default it never buys a bigger stack than you still need, and a hard sanity ceiling caps the price even with no cap set. {"Author":"dajoey","Name":"AutoPotion","Punchline":"Per-job HP, MP, and deep dungeon potion automation.","Description":"Auto-uses the highest-tier HP potion, MP potion (Ether), and the deep dungeon regen potion (Sustaining / Eurekan / Orthos / Pilgrim's) at configurable thresholds. Each potion's threshold and on/off state is stored per-job, so casters and tanks can have completely different setups.","InternalName":"AutoPotion","AssemblyVersion":"0.2.5.2","Changelog":"v0.2.5.2 (2026-10-10) [testing]
- **Automatic item uses no longer cancel an open action sequence.** Any potion, ether, deep dungeon medicine or Echo Drops that would land while mudra seals or Ten Chi Jin are held is delayed until the sequence completes, instead of cancelling the ninjutsu mid-chain. The delay lasts only while the sequence is up (a mudra window is about six seconds) and lifts immediately after; at or below 25% HP the heal fires regardless - a cancelled jutsu is cheaper than dying. No other job's behaviour changes.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- With the optional decision log enabled, a held use is recorded with the `heldmudra` near-miss reason, rate-limited like every other near-miss line.

v0.2.5.1 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the master switch, "Only in combat", "Only in a duty", the HP, MP and Regen potion switches with their thresholds, and Cure Silence (Echo Drops) to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- The potion settings apply to the active job's profile, as in the settings window.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.2.5.0 (2026-09-05)

- New per-job option: "Auto-use Echo Drops when silenced". When it is on and Silence lands (mob silence spells, AoE silences, deep dungeon traps), AutoPotion uses Echo Drops from inventory to cure it automatically. Item use is not blocked by Silence, so the cure works exactly when nothing else can.
- OFF by default like every option, and per job like the rest: tick the new box in the settings window for the jobs it should apply to. With it off (the default) nothing changes - not even a status check.
- It reuses the same machinery as the potions: HQ Echo Drops are preferred over normal ones, the shared 750 ms cooldown after any potion use applies, and a Silence that arrives during that cooldown is cured on the next tick.
- If the diagnostic tap is enabled, the cure logs as an `e` event; when it cannot fire the near-miss reasons are `edblocked` (on cooldown / blocked) or `ednostock` (none in the bags).
- No change to potion behaviour. HP/MP/regen thresholds, the overshoot guard, the deep dungeon Rehabilitation lockout and the in-combat / in-duty gates all work exactly as before.

v0.2.4.0 (2026-09-05)

- Added an optional "Log potion decisions" diagnostic, OFF by default. Turn it on with `/autopotion telemetry on` or the new Advanced / Diagnostics section of the settings window, and AutoPotion writes one line to its plugin log every time it uses a potion, plus a rate-limited line when a threshold was crossed and nothing fired.
- Purpose: the log line records the HP%, the MP%, the threshold that was in force and the job, so a threshold can be verified after the fact instead of guessed at. Nothing leaves the machine - the lines only go to the local Dalamud plugin log.
- The "nothing fired" lines say WHY in a short code: `hpover` (a potion was available but the heal would have been wasted), `hpblocked` / `mpblocked` / `rgblocked` (on cooldown or blocked by a status), `hpnostock` / `mpnostock` / `rgnostock` (none left in inventory) and `rgrehab` (Rehabilitation still up in a deep dungeon).
- These lines are heavily rate-limited on purpose: a repeated state logs once, not once per frame. Measured against 214 minutes of real play the near-miss lines come out under one line per minute, so the log stays readable.
- No change to potion behaviour. Thresholds, per-job profiles, the overshoot guard, the deep dungeon Rehabilitation lockout and the in-combat / in-duty gates all work exactly as before, and with the setting off (the default) the plugin does not even build a log line.

v0.2.3.0 (2026-09-05)

- Added the in-game "What's new" popup. After AutoPotion updates, its changelog now opens once inside the game so the changes are visible without a trip to GitHub. It waits until the character is logged in and out of combat, duty, cutscenes and zoning; closing it (Got it, X or Escape) marks it read. Type `/autopotion changelog` any time to reopen it.
- No change to potion behaviour: thresholds, per-job profiles and the in-combat / in-duty gates all work exactly as before.

  /bocchi → Opens the main window
  /bocchi config → Opens config (aliases: cfg, c)
  /bocchi config list → Lists config keys
  /bocchi config get <key> → Prints a config value
  /bocchi config set <key> <value> → Sets a config value

  /bocchi tp [fate|ce|pot] → Teleport toward nearest matching activity
  /bocchi illegal [on|off|toggle] → Control Illegal Mode (no arg opens the window)
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-ce → Flag registering CE on the map
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-fate → Flag a FATE on the map
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-non-pot-fate → Flag a non-pot FATE

{"Author":"Akari","Name":"Mahjong Advisor","InternalName":"Mahjong.Advisor.Plugin","AssemblyVersion":"0.4.4.0","TestingAssemblyVersion":"0.4.4.0","IsTestingExclusive":false,"RepoUrl":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor","ApplicableVersion":"any","DalamudApiLevel":15,"TestingDalamudApiLevel":15,"MinimumDalamudVersion":null,"Tags":["mahjong","doman","gold-saucer","auto-play","advisor"],"CategoryTags":["Utility"],"Punchline":"Discard advice and optional auto-play for Doman Mahjong.","Description":"Reads your Doman Mahjong hand, discards, dora, scores and called melds, then ranks each discard by hand speed against deal-in risk. Auto-play and file logging are on by default in this build: sit at a casual table and it plays, then /mjadv bundle packages the logs for support. /mjadv stop or the Automation tab returns to manual suggestions instantly. Discard piles and meld strips are found automatically; the node tools are only a fallback.","Changelog":"v0.4.4.0: Chi picker freeze fix. When a call prompt's claimed tile could not be identified, the single-shape chi gate counted shapes for the wrong tile: each candidate offered one run, but the actual tile completed two, so the game opened its shape-selection dialog - which ignores call callbacks - and the match froze (live at South 4 while leading 38,400; bundle 20261030-081345). Chi now fires only when the claim is pinned to one tile, or when every tile that could legally be on offer completes exactly one run; anything else passes instead. The picker-stall warning also logs once rather than every frame. The stale Advisor block that earlier builds wrote into the plugin config is no longer serialised: it was never read, is ignored on load, and disappears at the next config save. An experimental rollout-search re-ranking of discard candidates is included but ships OFF: a 240-match paired simulator A/B (two seeds) rejected it - it traded a 39% relative win-rate drop for nothing - so it stays a foundation for later work. v0.4.3.0: Result-screen retry. The result panel can swallow the first advance callback while it animates; the controller fired it twice and then its acted guard blocked every retry, leaving the screen waiting indefinitely (live Advanced freeze, state 29 unresolved for 12s). Advances now retry every 2.5 seconds while the result state persists, capped at 8 attempts so the deliberately manual match-end screen is not spammed. v0.4.2.0: Match-level tuning. A full hanchan evaluator now plays East+South with real score accounting, dealer rotation, honcha, riichi sticks and placement, and 120 paired matches showed the old risk settings were too passive. Win value 1800 and deal-in cost 4000 beat 1300/5200 on identical deals (average place 2.55 vs 2.65, more firsts, fewer fourths) with the deal-in rate unchanged at 9.3%. A v7 config migration applies the new values. Riichi hand value and placement stance were also tested and left unchanged - both were flat across 60-match arms. v0.4.1.0: Advanced-table defence. Cross-seat genbutsu now uses the pond lengths captured at the instant a riichi marker appears; the old turn-count shortcut broke once calls shortened ponds and could mark a tile discarded before the riichi as safe. Two declared riichi also force a fold for any hand that is not tenpai, overriding the placement chase. The simulator now records the same declaration snapshots: over 1,000 hands the defence fix moved deal-in rate from 10.3% to 9.5% and average points from -22 to +17, while the double-riichi rail was neutral there because the simulation has no placement stance. Live Advanced trial on 0.4.0.0 finished 1st, 4th, then leading when stopped; the 4th lost two deal-ins to one riichi player, the second 12,000 while two were in riichi. v0.4.0.0: Exact scoring core. Completed hands are now scored by yaku, fu, dora and the payment table (closed and open, riichi through yakuman), and the offline simulator uses that scoring for win legality and payouts. Ready-hand valuation was built and benchmarked but stays out of live decisions: over 1,500 simulated hands, mixing exact tenpai values with the existing one-away estimate cut the win rate from 15.4% to 8.1%, so the value scale must be unified for every shanten first. Advice is memoised per table state so the overlay and controller do not recompute the same decision. v0.3.10.0: Silent-endgame defence. The threat model measured a silent opponent as at most 19% likely tenpai, so on a table with no riichi and no melds every safety rule stayed off - the controller pushed one-away hands with 6-9 tiles left to draw into damaten twice in one match (4,200 and 2,200 deal-ins) and paid full tsumo on 14,300 and 20,000 hands. Silent seats now take on a readiness floor that rises from zero at wall 32 to a concrete threat at wall 16, arming the existing late-wall fold and per-tile safety ranking on quiet tables. v0.3.9.0: Chi freeze fixed. The shape-selection dialog ignores scripted call picks (confirmed by the first picker dump), so chi now only fires when exactly one shape is possible - that path completes with no dialog. Multi-shape chi passes instead of stalling; the pass log records how many shapes were declined. v0.3.8.0: Late-wall defence. When an opponent is a concrete threat and the wall is down to the last four go-arounds, the controller folds any hand that is not tenpai instead of pushing a 1-shanten no-riichi hand. This was the 12,000 deal-in in the first match. Diagnostic bundles now also include chi picker dumps. The end-of-match results screen still waits for you by design - that is the one click after a match. v0.3.7.0: Chi is now fully automated. The controller calls chi when the advisor ranks it best, and if the client shows the shape-selection surface it fires the first variant and re-evaluates the hand. The picker layout is dumped once per session to the log folder so shape-specific selection can be refined against real captures. A v6 config migration enables chi. v0.3.6.0: Read each opponent meld strip independently. A hidden empty strip for one quiet seat no longer suppresses every visible meld on the table, so the threat model sees called sets when they exist. This is a readiness/defence accuracy change; automation logic is unchanged. v0.3.5.0: Fix the second freeze. A complete open hand is no longer assumed to be a legal tsumo: the controller checks for an actual yaku and keeps discarding when there is none. Call prompts now prefer the newest board addition over a possibly stale pond tile (the live log claimed 6z/dragon while the actual Pon was 9m), and the log records the last discard tile/seat. A v5 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging. v0.3.4.0: Fix the self-kan freeze. A Kan/Pass bar at state 6 is ignored and the normal discard proceeds instead of firing a Pass callback the client ignores. Session stats are preserved after /mjadv stop so the bundle still shows the run, and a v4 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging for the next launch. v0.3.3.0: Reset the exposed tuning sliders to the fitted win-rate defaults (base hand value 1300, deal-in 5200, noten 1500, opponent hand 4000) with a one-time v3 config migration. Diagnostic bundles now include the actual Dalamud plugin config file from pluginConfigs. v0.3.2.0: State 15 is now treated as the generic other-players state unless real call buttons are present, state 22 (forced riichi discard) is automated, and state 27 (between-hands result/score) is recognised instead of showing stale advice. Overlay/advice are now gated to actual decision states, and diagnostic bundles can read the Dalamud log while it is open. v0.3.1.0: Auto-play and file logging are now on by default, /mjadv session starts a clean logged session, and /mjadv bundle packages the recent JSONL logs, config, layouts, Dalamud log tail and a full last-read snapshot into one zip. Status changes are now logged as auto-status records. v0.3.0.1: Re-arm auto-play on a state change even when the hand happens to repeat, and wait for the Riichi/Pass prompt to close before cutting the riichi tile. v0.3.0.0: Optional auto-play. Replays the client's FireCallback protocol for discards, calls, riichi, ron/tsumo and result advancement, using the reference solver's live-verified handshake and timing guards. Off by default; /mjadv auto [on/off] or /mjadv stop toggles it. Pon/ron/tsumo/riichi are enabled by default, chi and kan are opt-in, the chi shape picker pauses for a manual choice, and the new-hand screen is never auto-advanced. Added /mjadv hand and /mjadv options diagnostics. v0.2.0.2: Keep the previous wall count, so the wall-jump half of new-hand detection actually fires. v0.2.0.1: Reset the pond baselines at the start of a new hand, so the first discard of the hand is tracked and the first call prompt gets the right claimed tile. v0.2.0.0: Meld containers now read by default (112-115 families), with a fail-closed check against our own called-meld count. Own meld tiles are recovered from hand deltas when nodes are unavailable, so ukeire no longer counts tiles already in a call. Riichi detection is marker-node only; the dead rotation and score-drop paths are gone. One node-tree walk per read instead of up to seven. Fixed dead hands getting a nonzero win rate and Pass inventing a yaku path. Red-five decoding accepts both absolute and alias ids. Removed the obsolete fold-threshold setting. Setup window no longer reopens every launch. Added /mjadv melds diagnostics and richer log records.","DownloadLinkInstall":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor/releases/latest/download/MahjongAdvisor.zip","DownloadLinkTesting":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor/releases/latest/download/MahjongAdvisor.zip","DownloadLinkUpdate":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor/releases/latest/download/MahjongAdvisor.zip","LoadRequiredState":0,"LoadSync":false,"CanUnloadAsync":false,"LoadPriority":0,"AcceptsFeedback":true,"IsHide":false,"_SourceId":"dexcss-dalamudplugins","_SourceName":"dexcss / DalamudPlugins","_SourceUrl":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dexcss/DalamudPlugins/main/repo.json","_Category":"automation"}

{"Author":"MacaronDream, DhogGPT, XA","Name":"Questionable Companion","InternalName":"QSTCompanion","AssemblyVersion":"1.1.32.0","Description":"Automated character rotation and quest sequence execution for Questionable.

Automates multi-character MSQ progression by intelligently switching between characters based on quest completion and level requirements. Features include:
- Automatic character switching and quest tracking
- MSQ progression monitoring across all characters
- Allied Society quest rotation and prioritization
- Event quest automation with prerequisite checking
- Chauffeur Mode for following main character through quests

{"Author":"Akari","Name":"Mahjong Advisor","InternalName":"Mahjong.Advisor.Plugin","AssemblyVersion":"0.4.4.0","TestingAssemblyVersion":"0.4.4.0","IsTestingExclusive":false,"RepoUrl":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor","ApplicableVersion":"any","DalamudApiLevel":15,"TestingDalamudApiLevel":15,"MinimumDalamudVersion":null,"Tags":["mahjong","doman","gold-saucer","auto-play","advisor"],"CategoryTags":["Utility"],"Punchline":"Discard advice and optional auto-play for Doman Mahjong.","Description":"Reads your Doman Mahjong hand, discards, dora, scores and called melds, then ranks each discard by hand speed against deal-in risk. Auto-play and file logging are on by default in this build: sit at a casual table and it plays, then /mjadv bundle packages the logs for support. /mjadv stop or the Automation tab returns to manual suggestions instantly. Discard piles and meld strips are found automatically; the node tools are only a fallback.","Changelog":"v0.4.4.0: Chi picker freeze fix. When a call prompt's claimed tile could not be identified, the single-shape chi gate counted shapes for the wrong tile: each candidate offered one run, but the actual tile completed two, so the game opened its shape-selection dialog - which ignores call callbacks - and the match froze (live at South 4 while leading 38,400; bundle 20261030-081345). Chi now fires only when the claim is pinned to one tile, or when every tile that could legally be on offer completes exactly one run; anything else passes instead. The picker-stall warning also logs once rather than every frame. The stale Advisor block that earlier builds wrote into the plugin config is no longer serialised: it was never read, is ignored on load, and disappears at the next config save. An experimental rollout-search re-ranking of discard candidates is included but ships OFF: a 240-match paired simulator A/B (two seeds) rejected it - it traded a 39% relative win-rate drop for nothing - so it stays a foundation for later work. v0.4.3.0: Result-screen retry. The result panel can swallow the first advance callback while it animates; the controller fired it twice and then its acted guard blocked every retry, leaving the screen waiting indefinitely (live Advanced freeze, state 29 unresolved for 12s). Advances now retry every 2.5 seconds while the result state persists, capped at 8 attempts so the deliberately manual match-end screen is not spammed. v0.4.2.0: Match-level tuning. A full hanchan evaluator now plays East+South with real score accounting, dealer rotation, honcha, riichi sticks and placement, and 120 paired matches showed the old risk settings were too passive. Win value 1800 and deal-in cost 4000 beat 1300/5200 on identical deals (average place 2.55 vs 2.65, more firsts, fewer fourths) with the deal-in rate unchanged at 9.3%. A v7 config migration applies the new values. Riichi hand value and placement stance were also tested and left unchanged - both were flat across 60-match arms. v0.4.1.0: Advanced-table defence. Cross-seat genbutsu now uses the pond lengths captured at the instant a riichi marker appears; the old turn-count shortcut broke once calls shortened ponds and could mark a tile discarded before the riichi as safe. Two declared riichi also force a fold for any hand that is not tenpai, overriding the placement chase. The simulator now records the same declaration snapshots: over 1,000 hands the defence fix moved deal-in rate from 10.3% to 9.5% and average points from -22 to +17, while the double-riichi rail was neutral there because the simulation has no placement stance. Live Advanced trial on 0.4.0.0 finished 1st, 4th, then leading when stopped; the 4th lost two deal-ins to one riichi player, the second 12,000 while two were in riichi. v0.4.0.0: Exact scoring core. Completed hands are now scored by yaku, fu, dora and the payment table (closed and open, riichi through yakuman), and the offline simulator uses that scoring for win legality and payouts. Ready-hand valuation was built and benchmarked but stays out of live decisions: over 1,500 simulated hands, mixing exact tenpai values with the existing one-away estimate cut the win rate from 15.4% to 8.1%, so the value scale must be unified for every shanten first. Advice is memoised per table state so the overlay and controller do not recompute the same decision. v0.3.10.0: Silent-endgame defence. The threat model measured a silent opponent as at most 19% likely tenpai, so on a table with no riichi and no melds every safety rule stayed off - the controller pushed one-away hands with 6-9 tiles left to draw into damaten twice in one match (4,200 and 2,200 deal-ins) and paid full tsumo on 14,300 and 20,000 hands. Silent seats now take on a readiness floor that rises from zero at wall 32 to a concrete threat at wall 16, arming the existing late-wall fold and per-tile safety ranking on quiet tables. v0.3.9.0: Chi freeze fixed. The shape-selection dialog ignores scripted call picks (confirmed by the first picker dump), so chi now only fires when exactly one shape is possible - that path completes with no dialog. Multi-shape chi passes instead of stalling; the pass log records how many shapes were declined. v0.3.8.0: Late-wall defence. When an opponent is a concrete threat and the wall is down to the last four go-arounds, the controller folds any hand that is not tenpai instead of pushing a 1-shanten no-riichi hand. This was the 12,000 deal-in in the first match. Diagnostic bundles now also include chi picker dumps. The end-of-match results screen still waits for you by design - that is the one click after a match. v0.3.7.0: Chi is now fully automated. The controller calls chi when the advisor ranks it best, and if the client shows the shape-selection surface it fires the first variant and re-evaluates the hand. The picker layout is dumped once per session to the log folder so shape-specific selection can be refined against real captures. A v6 config migration enables chi. v0.3.6.0: Read each opponent meld strip independently. A hidden empty strip for one quiet seat no longer suppresses every visible meld on the table, so the threat model sees called sets when they exist. This is a readiness/defence accuracy change; automation logic is unchanged. v0.3.5.0: Fix the second freeze. A complete open hand is no longer assumed to be a legal tsumo: the controller checks for an actual yaku and keeps discarding when there is none. Call prompts now prefer the newest board addition over a possibly stale pond tile (the live log claimed 6z/dragon while the actual Pon was 9m), and the log records the last discard tile/seat. A v5 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging. v0.3.4.0: Fix the self-kan freeze. A Kan/Pass bar at state 6 is ignored and the normal discard proceeds instead of firing a Pass callback the client ignores. Session stats are preserved after /mjadv stop so the bundle still shows the run, and a v4 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging for the next launch. v0.3.3.0: Reset the exposed tuning sliders to the fitted win-rate defaults (base hand value 1300, deal-in 5200, noten 1500, opponent hand 4000) with a one-time v3 config migration. Diagnostic bundles now include the actual Dalamud plugin config file from pluginConfigs. v0.3.2.0: State 15 is now treated as the generic other-players state unless real call buttons are present, state 22 (forced riichi discard) is automated, and state 27 (between-hands result/score) is recognised instead of showing stale advice. Overlay/advice are now gated to actual decision states, and diagnostic bundles can read the Dalamud log while it is open. v0.3.1.0: Auto-play and file logging are now on by default, /mjadv session starts a clean logged session, and /mjadv bundle packages the recent JSONL logs, config, layouts, Dalamud log tail and a full last-read snapshot into one zip. Status changes are now logged as auto-status records. v0.3.0.1: Re-arm auto-play on a state change even when the hand happens to repeat, and wait for the Riichi/Pass prompt to close before cutting the riichi tile. v0.3.0.0: Optional auto-play. Replays the client's FireCallback protocol for discards, calls, riichi, ron/tsumo and result advancement, using the reference solver's live-verified handshake and timing guards. Off by default; /mjadv auto [on/off] or /mjadv stop toggles it. Pon/ron/tsumo/riichi are enabled by default, chi and kan are opt-in, the chi shape picker pauses for a manual choice, and the new-hand screen is never auto-advanced. Added /mjadv hand and /mjadv options diagnostics. v0.2.0.2: Keep the previous wall count, so the wall-jump half of new-hand detection actually fires. v0.2.0.1: Reset the pond baselines at the start of a new hand, so the first discard of the hand is tracked and the first call prompt gets the right claimed tile. v0.2.0.0: Meld containers now read by default (112-115 families), with a fail-closed check against our own called-meld count. Own meld tiles are recovered from hand deltas when nodes are unavailable, so ukeire no longer counts tiles already in a call. Riichi detection is marker-node only; the dead rotation and score-drop paths are gone. One node-tree walk per read instead of up to seven. Fixed dead hands getting a nonzero win rate and Pass inventing a yaku path. Red-five decoding accepts both absolute and alias ids. Removed the obsolete fold-threshold setting. Setup window no longer reopens every launch. Added /mjadv melds diagnostics and richer log records.","DownloadLinkInstall":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor/releases/latest/download/MahjongAdvisor.zip","DownloadLinkTesting":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor/releases/latest/download/MahjongAdvisor.zip","DownloadLinkUpdate":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor/releases/latest/download/MahjongAdvisor.zip","LoadRequiredState":0,"LoadSync":false,"CanUnloadAsync":false,"LoadPriority":0,"AcceptsFeedback":true,"IsHide":false,"_SourceId":"dexcss-dalamudplugins","_SourceName":"dexcss / DalamudPlugins","_SourceUrl":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dexcss/DalamudPlugins/main/repo.json"}
